system_configurations.name: RCCL-AINIC-TW-GFX950
system_configurations.description: RCCL AINIC (RoCE) test plan for the TensorWave gfx950 (MI355X) cluster. Two categories: 'gtest-tests' (NetIbMPI + GIN component/unit gtests, 2 nodes x 1 GPU = 2 ranks) and 'rccl-tests-sweeps' (NCCL_NET plugin x knobs perf sweeps and IONIC hardware counter validation on rccl-tests, 2 nodes x 8 GPU = 16 ranks). The category (and which binary directory a suite uses) is derived from is_gtest, so no per-suite lane field is needed. Run with --system ainic. Scope: --scope smoke runs the fast subset ('smoke': true); --scope nightly (or no --scope) runs all enabled suites.

mpi_args.ainic: --bind-to numa --mca pml ob1 --mca osc ^ucx --mca btl tcp,self --mca btl_tcp_if_include eno0

qpshare_base.description: QP-sharing base (RCCL_IB_QP_SHARING_ENABLE master switch + RCCL_IB_COMM_NGROUPS). No tests here; children extend and set the tunables. NIC merging is turned off because the suite connects on device 0 and reasons about one physical IB device per rank. The CAST scheduler is deliberately left off: the QP-sharing tests skip themselves when RCCL_IB_QP_SCHED_ENABLE=1, so these configs extend gtest_base rather than cast_base. RCCL_IB_QP_SHARING_ENABLE, RCCL_IB_COMM_NGROUPS and RCCL_IB_QP_DEPTH_MULTIPLIER are all RCCL_PARAMs and are cached for the process lifetime, which is why each value is a separate config rather than a case inside one run. RCCL_IB_QP_SHARING_VALIDATE_POOL=1 runs IbCastValidateSharedQpPool each time the plugin's last finalize() drops netRefCount to 0 (every test's TearDown), so a leaked pool slot or commId is reported by the suite whose subject is pool bookkeeping; in a debug build its assert aborts the binary on the first leak.

qpshare_ngroups1.description: A17: QP sharing at NGROUPS=1 — every connection is assigned to group 0, so the whole functional set runs on a single shared QP. RCCL_IB_QP_DEPTH_MULTIPLIER=8 scales the shared QP's CQ and work-queue sizing so the configuration is not close to the queue-depth limit at these connection counts.

tests.name: A17_QpShare_AlgoLayoutSweep
tests.description: Group-assignment layout, state only, no data phase. Opens connections one at a time up to min(2*NGROUPS+1, 64) and compares every live comm against the reference model (test/transport/NetIbMPI/QpShareRefModel.hpp) after each create — sharedGroupIdx, isSharedQpPrimary, refcount, cqRefcount, commId, and the cross-comm QP-identity relation — then tears down in creation order, releasing each group's PRIMARY while its SECONDARYs are live, re-checking after each destroy. Expectations are derived from RCCL_IB_COMM_NGROUPS rather than pinned to one value.

tests.name: A17_QpShare_AlgoChurnLayout
tests.description: Group assignment under interleaved create/destroy with rotating non-tail victims, so a comm is released while it still has live neighbours in its group. Re-validates the full layout against the reference model after every operation, which is where a refcount that survives teardown or a pool slot that is freed but still counted becomes visible. Group spread is measured and reported, never asserted.

tests.name: A17_QpShare_DataAllConnsTransfer
tests.description: Data path at this (NGROUPS, DEPTH_MULTIPLIER) point: opens QPSHARE_TEST_NCONNS connections (default derived from NGROUPS) and moves data on every one of them across a payload sweep of 0, 1, 127, 128, 4095, 4096, 65535, 65536 and 1 MiB bytes, pattern-verified per connection.

tests.name: A17_QpShare_DataUnsharedGroups
tests.description: The unshared regime as an explicit case rather than a skip: the connection count is derived as min(NGROUPS, 8) so occupancy-modulo gives every comm a group of its own. Asserts each comm is a solo PRIMARY on a distinct physical QP and exercises the data path on each.

tests.name: A17_QpShare_DataFlushRouting
tests.description: GDR flush completion routing over a shared CQ. A flush QP is per-comm and is not itself shared, but its completion lands on the group's shared CQ. Locates a PRIMARY/SECONDARY pair from the reference model rather than hardcoded indices, posts iflush() on both, and waits the SECONDARY first so completions are exercised against commId routing rather than post order. An unshared comm supplies the baseline. Requires GDR-capable hardware and skips otherwise.

qpshare_ngroups2.description: A18: QP sharing at NGROUPS=2 — the smallest value that mixes a PRIMARY-only group with a PRIMARY+SECONDARY group, so group-index arithmetic has more than one possible answer. Same five functional tests as A17.

tests.name: A18_QpShare_AlgoLayoutSweep
tests.description: Group-assignment layout at NGROUPS=2, state only. See A17 for what the sweep checks; the connection count and every expectation are re-derived from NGROUPS.

tests.name: A18_QpShare_AlgoChurnLayout
tests.description: Interleaved create/destroy with rotating non-tail victims at NGROUPS=2, layout re-validated against the reference model after every operation.

tests.name: A18_QpShare_DataAllConnsTransfer
tests.description: Payload sweep from 0 to 1 MiB on every connection at NGROUPS=2, pattern-verified per connection.

tests.name: A18_QpShare_DataUnsharedGroups
tests.description: Unshared regime at NGROUPS=2: two connections, one solo PRIMARY per group, each on its own physical QP.

tests.name: A18_QpShare_DataFlushRouting
tests.description: GDR flush completion routing over a shared CQ at NGROUPS=2, with an unshared comm as baseline. Skips on hardware without GDR.

qpshare_ngroups16.description: A19: QP sharing at NGROUPS=16 — the wide point. The connection counts the tests derive straddle the shared and unshared regimes within one run, and the layout sweep reaches 33 connections across 16 groups. Same five functional tests as A17.

tests.name: A19_QpShare_AlgoLayoutSweep
tests.description: Group-assignment layout across 16 groups, state only: 33 connections created and torn down one at a time, full layout re-checked after every operation.

tests.name: A19_QpShare_AlgoChurnLayout
tests.description: Interleaved create/destroy with rotating non-tail victims across 16 groups — the widest point at which occupancy-modulo assignment is exercised against the reference model.

tests.name: A19_QpShare_DataAllConnsTransfer
tests.description: Payload sweep from 0 to 1 MiB on every connection at NGROUPS=16, pattern-verified per connection.

tests.name: A19_QpShare_DataUnsharedGroups
tests.description: Unshared regime at NGROUPS=16: the connection count is capped at 8, so every comm is a solo PRIMARY on its own physical QP.

tests.name: A19_QpShare_DataFlushRouting
tests.description: GDR flush completion routing over a shared CQ at NGROUPS=16, with an unshared comm as baseline. Skips on hardware without GDR.

qpshare_depth_ceiling.description: A20: shared-QP depth-multiplier sizing. RCCL_IB_QP_DEPTH_MULTIPLIER scales the shared CQ, which is sized 3 x NET_IB_MAX_REQUESTS(256) x NCCL_IB_QPS_PER_CONNECTION x multiplier entries, so the multiplier and the QP count multiply into the same device limit and both are pinned here. 96 with QPS=1 requests a CQ far larger than the default and covers how the transport sizes that CQ against the device's queried max_cqe. QPSHARE_TEST_NCONNS=2 keeps the run to the sizing question rather than connection volume. The usable multiplier is hardware-dependent (a function of the device's max_cqe), so this value is a probe of the sizing path, not a portable constant.

tests.name: A20_QpShare_DataAllConnsTransfer_DepthCeiling
tests.description: Two connections in one group at a depth multiplier of 96, exercising shared-CQ sizing and the data path at that setting.

qpshare_stress.description: A21: QP-sharing scale and resource lifetime. NGROUPS=2 with DEPTH_MULTIPLIER=64 and one QP per connection, so the shared QP carries the queue depth the default connection counts require. Scale with QPSHARE_TEST_NCONNS and QPSHARE_TEST_ITERS. Connection churn is intentionally not in this config — it runs separately as A22.

tests.name: A21_QpShare_StressManyConns
tests.description: Sustained batched traffic over QPSHARE_TEST_NCONNS connections to one peer (default 100, so roughly 50 comms per shared QP at NGROUPS=2). Each connection sends 20 messages of 4 KiB and the received data is compared byte-for-byte.

tests.name: A21_QpShare_StressSharedRqSaturation
tests.description: Loads the shared receive queue: one message posted from every connection before any completion is waited on, repeated for QPSHARE_TEST_ITERS rounds (default 10) over QPSHARE_TEST_NCONNS connections (default 50), with per-round pattern verification.

tests.name: A21_QpShare_StressBatchCreateDestroy
tests.description: Bursty lifecycle: QPSHARE_TEST_ITERS batches (default 110) of QPSHARE_TEST_NCONNS connections (default 10) created together, used, and destroyed together. Every batch starts from an empty live set, so at each checkpoint the layout is re-derived from a fresh reference model and RDMA object counts are compared against a pre-batch baseline. Because several comms are live at once, the batch size has to fit the configured depth multiplier.

qpshare_stress_churn.description: A22: sequential connection churn under QP sharing, isolated in its own config so it runs in a separate process from A21 and its result is reported independently. Long-running by design — the default 2048 connect/transfer/close cycles are minutes of wall time, hence the 1800s timeout.

tests.name: A22_QpShare_StressConnectionChurn
tests.description: QPSHARE_TEST_ITERS connect/transfer/close cycles (default 2048) with exactly one connection live at a time, so every cycle is fully torn down before the next begins and each teardown reaches the group-release path. RDMA object counts and the comm's pool state are checkpointed every quarter of the run against a pre-churn baseline. Sharing depth is 1 by construction here: the test covers the create/destroy lifecycle of a shared group, not concurrent occupancy.

qpshare_heap_poison.description: A23: QP-sharing group teardown under glibc heap poisoning. Same test and tunables as A19; the addition is MALLOC_PERTURB_=165, which makes glibc overwrite freed heap with 0xa5, so any read through a pointer into a freed comm returns poison instead of whatever the allocator happened to leave behind. MALLOC_PERTURB_ is a glibc feature and is inert on other allocators, so on a non-glibc platform this config is equivalent to A19.

tests.name: A23_QpShare_AlgoChurnLayout_HeapPoison
tests.description: Interleaved create/destroy across 16 groups with freed heap poisoned, exercising the shared-QP group teardown path against pointers that may outlive the comm they point into.

rccl_tests_base.description: Category 'rccl-tests-sweeps': prebuilt rccl-tests perf binaries under PERF_BIN_DIR that load the fresh librccl.so at runtime via LD_LIBRARY_PATH. Sets NO shared env_variables so each sweep runs against stock defaults plus its own per-suite knobs, and NO group-level command_args by design - every test sets its own explicit, complete command_args so nothing is silently concatenated/duplicated.

cts_force_override.description: PR #4657 force-override precedence. RCCL_CTS_OFFLOAD_ENABLED=1 is the strongest override and forces CTS offload on ALL connections including P2P, overriding RCCL_IB_P2P_DISABLE_CTS=1. Exercises the `enabled && (userForced || !(isP2p && IbP2pDisableCts))` userForced branch that no other sweep suite covers.

tests.name: B11_alltoall_ROCMIB_CTSforceOverride
tests.description: PR #4657: RCCL_CTS_OFFLOAD_ENABLED=1 overrides IB_P2P_DISABLE_CTS=1, forcing CTS on P2P - validates the force-override precedence.

tests.name: B11_allreduce_ROCMIB_CTSforceOverride
tests.description: PR #4657 force-override on collective transport: allreduce expected PASS (CTS is supported on collective connections).

opt_recv_completion.description: Optional recv completion with CTS offload on. RCCL_IB_OPTIONAL_RECV_COMPLETION=0 so CTS offload is the only thing that enables the skip. QP sched off. Allreduce pins NCCL_PROTO so net.cc plants NCCL_NET_OPTIONAL_RECV_COMPLETION.

opt_recv_completion_no_cts.description: Optional recv completion with CTS offload off: the combination this PR newly makes reachable (control param on, not equivalent to useCtsOffload).

tests.name: B13_allreduce_optRecvCompletion_noCts_LL128
tests.description: Allreduce LL128 with optional recv completion and CTS offload off.

alltoall_fullrange_guard.description: Dedicated large-size alltoall guard for the AINIC data path: CAST and ROCM-IB swept over the full 1K-16G range with a plain-IB control. Test names use the 1K_16G suffix to match the actual -b 1K -e 16G range.

net_ib_gdr_flush_flag_base.description: Shared env for remote GDR flush flag suites. Carries no tests: extends merges test lists, so children would inherit them. NCCL_NET=IB: with RCCL_AINIC_ROCE=1 an unset NCCL_NET selects IB-CAST, which keeps the flag off.

tests.name: GdrFlushFlag_DefaultQps

tests.name: GdrFlushFlagTune_reduce_scatter

tests.name: GdrFlushFlagTune_reduce
tests.description: Reduce with the scaled-down Ring/LL128 pipeline chunk.

mseg_base.description: Shared env for the IB-MSEG multi-segment suites. Carries no tests: extends merges test lists, so children would inherit them. NCCL_NET=IB selects IB-MSEG under NCCL_MULTI_SEGMENT_REGISTER=1; with RCCL_AINIC_ROCE=1 an unset NCCL_NET selects IB-CAST. The whitebox GDR flush suites (net_ib_gdr_flush_mseg, net_ib_multisegment_flush) are not defined here because this config has no net_ib_gdr_flush suite; the 8-node hierarchical CE job needs more nodes than this cluster's lane.

net_ib_multisegment.description: IB-MSEG multi-segment DMA-BUF path: per-segment registration, asymmetric offsets, boundary splitting and the segment cap. One rank per node so the DeepEP multi-node stress test is not skipped; the fixture needs DMA-BUF export (NCCL_DMABUF_ENABLE from gtest_base) and GDR. UT_NET_IB_MSEG_REQUIRE_DMABUF=1 turns a missing DMA-BUF, VMM or dma-buf export API into a failure instead of a skip; every net_ib_multisegment job sets it. The flush tests are in net_ib_multisegment_flush because they need a non-default RCCL_PARAM.

tests.name: NetIB_MultiSeg_PerSegmentRegistrationAndTransfer
tests.description: Register a 4-segment VMM window through regMrDmaBuf with fd -1 (the plugin's segment walk) and move every segment end to end

tests.name: NetIB_MultiSeg_IntraSegmentOffsetSelection
tests.description: Transfers anchored at three offsets inside each segment: per-segment lkey/rkey selection must follow the address, not segment 0

tests.name: NetIB_MultiSeg_DeepEP_AsymmetricOffsetTransfer
tests.description: DeepEP-style per-peer window: sender starts in segment 1 while the receiver starts in segment 0, so a shared cursor would pick the wrong key

tests.name: NetIB_MultiSeg_CrossBoundaryTransferSucceeds
tests.description: One transfer straddling the seg0/seg1 boundary is split at the receiver's boundary using the per-segment rkeys from the CTS layout

tests.name: NetIB_MultiSeg_DeepEP_MultiNodeAsymmetricCrossBoundaryStress
tests.description: 32 iterations crossing independently selected source and destination boundaries in an 8-segment window, with a sentinel-checked destination; requires ranks on two nodes

tests.name: NetIB_MultiSeg_WholeBufferSingleTransfer
tests.description: A single transfer spanning the whole window crosses every boundary and exercises the full splitting builder

tests.name: NetIB_MultiSeg_ExceedsMaxSegmentsRejected
tests.description: A buffer with more than RCCL_IB_REG_SEG_DEFAULT segments is rejected with ncclInvalidUsage and produces no handle

tests.name: NetIB_MultiSeg_NonUniformLayoutRegisters
tests.description: A 2S, S, 2S window has no uniform segment stride and still registers, because the splitter accepts any layout

tests.name: NetIB_MultiSeg_SingleSegmentThroughMultiSegPath
tests.description: Regression: a 1-segment window through the multi-segment entry point still takes the nSegments==1 fast path

tests.name: NetIB_MultiSeg_HostAndDeviceSingleSegmentRegression
tests.description: Regression: plain host (NCCL_PTR_HOST) and device (NCCL_PTR_CUDA) registrations still transfer through the single-region path

tests.name: NetIB_MultiSeg_MultiRecvMixesSingleAndMultiSegmentHandles
tests.description: One multi-recv mixing a single-segment handle with a boundary-crossing multi-segment one, in both orders, so per-entry layout selection diverges within one WR chain

tests.name: NetIB_MultiSeg_ConcurrentPairs

tests.name: NetIB_MultiSeg_SendQueueFatChainOversubscribe

tests.name: NetIB_MultiSeg_ReceiverSideMatchingById
tests.description: Boundary-crossing transfers with ID-based receiver matching: a single receive whose chunk straddles a boundary must report the full size, not only the last slice carrying the imm

net_ib_multisegment_register_off.description: IB-MSEG (NCCL_NET=IB-MSEG) with NCCL_MULTI_SEGMENT_REGISTER=0: both ends keep the legacy CTS, a multi-segment receive registration is declined, and single-segment registrations still transfer.

tests.name: NetIB_MultiSeg_RegisterOff_DeclinesRegistration
tests.description: A 4-segment receive window is declined with ncclInvalidUsage because the comm has no CTS layout; the sender still registers

tests.name: NetIB_MultiSeg_RegisterOff_SingleSegmentRegression
tests.description: Host, device and 1-segment VMM registrations still transfer with the switch off

net_ib_multisegment_scale_2x4.description: IB-MSEG multi-segment transfers with 4 ranks on each of 2 nodes: 4 cross-node pairs, each on its own NIC, register and move multi-segment windows at once.

tests.name: NetIB_MultiSeg_ConcurrentPairs_2x4
tests.description: 4 concurrent cross-node pairs move chunks across every segment boundary

net_ib_multisegment_gdr_flush_flag.description: IB-MSEG segmented sends with the remote GDR flush flag on: every boundary-crossing receive must leave id + 1 in its QPs' flags.

net_ib_rma_multisegment.description: Multi-segment DMA-BUF RMA registration (AIRUNTIME-2351), 1 rank per node on 2 nodes. NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE gates segment enumeration, and each test checks that every rank's registered handle reports more than one segment; without that the tests would skip instead of exercising the per-segment path, so RCCL_TEST_RMA_MSEG_REQUIRE turns that skip into a failure. RCCL_MPI_LOG_ALL_RANKS keeps per-rank logs, since otherwise output from ranks other than 0 is discarded.

tests.description: Reproducer: a 4-segment VMM window registers per segment and moves data end to end

tests.name: NetIB_RMA_MultiSeg_PartialFinalSegment
tests.description: Two full mappings plus half of a third: the last MR is clipped to the requested range and a transfer ending at the last registered byte succeeds

tests.name: NetIB_RMA_MultiSeg_SubPageBounds

tests.name: NetIB_RMA_MultiSeg_IFlushSingleSegmentRegression

net_ib_rma_multisegment_hybrid.description: DeepEP HybridElasticSymmetricMemory windows ([GPU][CPU per local rank]). RCCL_TEST_HYBRID_VMM_REQUIRE turns a missing hybrid VMM runtime or a failed hybrid allocation into a failure instead of a skip.
